out_of_schema_notes: No set-point or NOR of the step changed at Version 2.0, so ProcessParameter.target_value and NOR are the values of the parameter table, which are also the values in force. ProcessParameter.PAR is the NOR-propagated PAR for MVM LRF, the range carried into the control strategy (PCMP-001 §7.6), which is also the intersection over the outputs with an adequate model. rationale_for_criticality carries the classification argument of the report, each parameter anchored on its own sentences of it.

The step forms no quality attribute. The QualityAttribute records are the two cumulative viral clearance attributes, to which the step contributes log reduction, and fragments, against whose drug substance criterion its filtrate is judged. acceptance_criteria holds the drug substance criterion of the CQA register and the Version 2.0 intermediate acceptance criterion of the step; acceptance_criteria (the annex layer) holds the rows of the criteria-change table, Version 1.0 superseded and Version 2.0 in force. Step yield is a process performance output with no criterion: the concept attr:step_yield.

proven_acceptable_ranges: the rows of the PAR table for MVM LRF and fragments, with par_at_setpoint and par_nor_propagated as the columns 'PAR (set-point)' and 'PAR (NOR)' print them, and the report's description of the two analyses in its own words, in report statements anchored on its sentences. XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and no PAR: its two rows (n.a.) anchor an explicit non-claim.

The schema has no record type for a discrepancy from the plan. PD-009-01 to PD-009-07 are report statements anchored on their rows of the discrepancy register; the studies they concern carry that row as a source reference.

The report records no deviation: a characterization study is not GMP manufacture, so the two events of execution are study events, under the numbers Version 1.0 gave them (DEV-009-01, DEV-009-02). They are Deviation records, the schema's only record type for an event of execution. no_impact_on_conclusions is true for DEV-009-01, which the report bounds in every case the record leaves open, and false for DEV-009-02, whose effect the report says cannot be assessed from the record.

Studies: every row of the execution-window table has a StudyDesign record. Only the two designs carry n_runs, which the corpus test reserves for the seeded DoE designs. The qualification compares step yield alone; the flux decay profile and the post-use integrity test it was planned to compare are not recorded (PD-009-03).

StatisticalModelFit: the planned full quadratic of each output with a criterion (the re-evaluation table, with the terms of Appendix C), the selected models of MVM LRF (passes the first three adequacy criteria, fails the criterion on residuals and influential runs, used for the ranges and the design space, PD-009-02), of XMuLV LRF (not adequate), of fragments and of step yield (intercept-only), and the four screening models. A p-value printed as '< 0.001' has no float value; its term carries significant=true. The deletion of every response-surface run in turn is in report statements, one per row of the deletion table.

parameter_impacts_attribute: filtration volume on MVM LRF, on its row of the coefficient table of the selected model. parameter_does_not_significantly_impact_attribute: every other parameter and output on its row of the screening effects table, with the full quadratic row for pressure on MVM LRF and the row of the selected (not adequate) model for pressure on XMuLV LRF.

The ModularContribution records are the platform claims of the step against the two cumulative requirements; cumulative_value is the sum of the platform claims the report states, not a measured clearance. The capability of the cumulative clearance is a property of the train.
The equipment id equip:vf_sdm follows the Version 1.0 report and the PCP-009 Version 2.0 annex.

process_steps.description: Step 9 of the A-Mab drug substance process. The step filters the flow-through pool of anion exchange through a membrane whose pore size distribution retains the parvoviruses while the antibody passes, at a set filtration pressure, in psi, up to a set filtration volume, the volume of load filtered per square metre of membrane, in L/m2. It removes virus by size, is the principal source of MVM clearance and also carries a claim for XMuLV, each of 4.62 log10 in the modular viral clearance claim. The step forms no quality attribute; its filtrate is judged against the drug substance criterion for fragments, because no later step changes them.
equipment: scale-down model of the commercial step

source_references.quote: The step removes virus by size.

It is the dedicated small virus removal operation of the purification train and the principal source of clearance of minute virus of mice (MVM), and it also carries a claim for xenotropic murine leukemia virus (XMuLV).
The small virus retentive filtration step filters the flow-through pool of anion exchange through a membrane whose pore size distribution retains the parvoviruses while the antibody passes.
The step is run at a set filtration pressure, in psi, up to a set filtration volume, which is the volume of load filtered per square metre of membrane, in L/m2.
The step forms no quality attribute.

parameters.rationale_for_criticality: Classified WC-CPP under SOP-4001 (PCP-009 §7, PCMP-001 §7.7). A term containing the parameter is significant for MVM LRF (p < 0.001); across the range studied the mean MVM LRF falls by 1.73 log10 and across its NOR-propagated PAR of 50–136 L/m2 by 1.65 log10, for an attribute of very high criticality. The PAR extends 31 L/m2 beyond the upper NOR edge and its lower edge is the end of the range studied; the volumetric load is set by the volume of load applied to a filter of known area, so it can be held within its NOR. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a number for the size of the effect or the margin, so the class is a judgement of the report on this margin and this control. With run 5 deleted the PAR would reach the end of the range studied and the class would be the same.

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 1: Scale-down model (objective 1). The qualification compared step yield alone, with an offset of −0.5 percentage points (90 % confidence interval −1.2 to 0.3). Flux decay and the post-use integrity test are not recorded, so objective 1 was not met as PCP-009 states it. PCP-009 §7 requires this report to state what “the scale-down model is qualified” means for this step, given the outputs that the qualification compares. Only step yield was compared, and it has no criterion, so no conclusion was decided by an offset. The outputs with a criterion are judged on the scale-down results, the LRF on the spiking model and fragments on the mechanism of the step.

source_references.quote: Scale-down model (objective 1).

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 2: Effects (objective 2). Filtration volume lowers the mean MVM LRF by 1.73 log10 across 50–140 L/m2. No effect of filtration pressure was detected on any output, and no effect of either parameter on XMuLV LRF, fragments or step yield.

source_references.quote: Effects (objective 2).

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 3: Models (objective 3). The selected model of MVM LRF passes the model F-test, shows no lack of fit and meets the limit on overfitting of PCMP-001 §7.2. It fails the criterion on residuals and influential runs on run 5, the axial run at 50 L/m2 and 19 psi. XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and is judged on its measured results. The selected models of fragments and step yield are intercept-only.

source_references.quote: Models (objective 3).

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 4: Proven acceptable ranges (objective 4). The NOR-propagated PAR of filtration volume is 50–136 L/m2 for MVM LRF and the whole range studied for fragments. The PAR of filtration pressure is the whole range studied, 8–30 psi, for both. Every PAR contains the NOR. XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and no PAR, and every measured result met its claim across the range studied.

source_references.quote: Proven acceptable ranges (objective 4).

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 5: Classification (objective 5). Both parameters are WC-CPP. The class of filtration pressure rests on the basis that the A-Mab case study gives and on the scope of the viral clearance claim, not on a detected effect.

source_references.quote: Classification (objective 5).

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 6: Criteria. Each output with a criterion met its intermediate acceptance criterion across the NOR, MVM LRF at 5.25 log10 against 4.62, XMuLV LRF on measured results from 5.90 log10 against 4.62, and fragments at 0.78 % against 2.00 %.

source_references.quote: Criteria.

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 7: Design space. The design space covers 91 % of the characterized region and excludes filtration volumes above 137.6 L/m2. Deleting run 5, the run at 50 L/m2 and 19 psi with the highest LRF at that volume, would carry the boundary to the end of the range studied.

source_references.quote: Design space.

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 8: Capability. The Cpk of the cumulative MVM clearance, 1.51, is the tightest of the attributes to which the step contributes, above the target of 1.33 and the minimum of 1.0. No simulated batch fell outside any criterion.

source_references.quote: Capability.

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 9: Success of the study. PCP-009 §7 asks for a qualified scale-down model, two viral clearance models accepted as predictive and a PAR containing the NOR for each parameter against each viral clearance response. The PARs of MVM LRF contain the NOR. The MVM model was used for prediction although it fails the criterion on residuals and influential runs (Section 13.2). The XMuLV model was not accepted, so XMuLV LRF has no PAR, and its measured results met the claim across the whole range studied. The qualification compared step yield alone. The success criterion is therefore not met in full.

source_references.quote: Success of the study.

statements.statement_text: Conclusion 10: Record. Every run of the two study events was retained, as Version 1.0 recorded. The record does not name the runs, so the deletion of each run in turn covers only an event that affected a single response-surface run (Section 13.1). The results roll up into PCMR-001.

source_references.quote: Record.
